sources.citation: OLAC. 2025. Resources in and about the Trimuris language (combined catalog, up-to-date 2025-11-04; Internet Archive copy 2025-11-17).
sources.note: The only primary item in the world's archives is 'Bagusa Trimurus Wordlist DeVries. DeVries, Jim (researcher). 1985. SIL International. oai:sil.org:68569' (Lexical resources). 'Language descriptions' = Glottolog entry only. No grammar, sketch, or phonology exists in OLAC.

sources.citation: Kluge, Angela. 2017. A grammar of Papuan Malay. (Studies in Diversity Linguistics 11.) Berlin: Language Science Press. sec. 1.4 p.13; Appendix C p.682.
sources.note: p.13: 'For the remaining eight languages no resources are available except for their listing in the Ethnologue (Lewis, Simons & Fennig 2016a) and Glottolog (Nordhoff et al. 2013): Bagusa, Betaf, Jofotek-Bromnya, Keijar, Kwerba Mamberamo, Kwinsu, Trimuris, and Wares.' Appendix C row 'Trimuris [tip]' has no survey/lexicon/grammar/literacy ticks.

sources.citation: Voorhoeve, C. L. 1975. Languages of Irian Jaya: Checklist. Preliminary classification, language maps, wordlists. Pacific Linguistics B-31. Canberra: ANU.
sources.note: 'Trimuris' / 'Nopuk' / 'Nupuk' do not occur anywhere in the text (a full-text search for stress/accent). Trimuris is not distinguished from Kwerba (no. 68). Wordlist key p.92: 'Stress and pitch are not indicated.'

sources.citation: Usher, Timothy. n.d. New Guinea World: Kwerba (Northwest New Guinea > Foja Range > West Foja Range > Apauwar River). Santa Fe Institute. (Internet Archive copy 2022-10-06; live site now login-walled.)
sources.note: Page 'under construction', no data. Its Kwerba-family source list is the fullest bibliography seen; the only Trimuris item is 'Donohue (2005: 427-428) reflexes of proto-Kwerba /*s/ with eight terms from Anggreso, Kwerba, Kasonaweja, Trimuris and Bagusa villages'. Also lists 'de Vries (1991) Kwerba (unobtained)' and 'Kim (1999) phonology of Kwerba of Aurimi village (unobtained)'. Nothing on stress.

sources.citation: Eberhard, David M., Gary F. Simons & Charles D. Fennig (eds.). 2019. Ethnologue: Languages of the World, 22nd ed., entry 'Trimuris'. Dallas: SIL International.
sources.note: Nothing on phonology. Pop. 300 (1999 SIL); Jayapura regency, Mamberamo Tengah, Mamberamo east bank; classification Tor-Kwerba > Greater Kwerba > Kwerba > Nuclear; 'Dialects: None known. Low intelligibility of Kwerba [kwe]. Lexical similarity: 70% with Kauwera [xau] and 60% with Kwerba [kwe].' Language resources: OLAC only.

sources.citation: Clouse, Duane, Mark Donohue & Felix Ma. 2002. Survey report of the north coast of Irian Jaya. SIL Electronic Survey Reports 2002-078. 18 pp.
sources.note: Trimuris appears only on the survey map (p.4) and as a leaf of the Kwerba-subfamily tree ('Bagusa Kwerba-Aurimi Trimuris Kauwera Kwerba-Mam.', p.10). Phonology notes (sec. 4.3) cover Airoran and Samarokena only. Nothing on Trimuris. References cite DeVries 1991 'Kwerba' ms and Kim 1999 'Kwerba phonology' ms (SIL Abepura).
